jamie (support): FYI ACME ticket — p99 for POST /v1/generate jumped from ~80ms -> ~1.2s starting 2026-03-16T18:22Z. They claim client region affinity to us-west-2, traces show egress via eu-west-2. Attached trace id 84f2a3c7f9. No 5xxs, responses still 200 but slow.

support-bot: created INC-2026-437 and linked customer thread <https://support.redwood/acme/INC-2026-437> :ticket: 

raj (sre): Can you paste the full trace spans and the model info? Also, any quota/autoscale events around 18:21-18:23Z?

jamie (support): Model: redwood/gpt-variant-3.large. Trace snip pasted below (full trace uploaded to tracer UI). No auth errors, tokens valid.

tracer-bot: trace 84f2a3c7f9 uploaded -> https://internal.redwood/traces/84f2a3c7f9

jamie (support): Trace (simplified):
```
client -> edge-us-west-2 (ingress) : 18ms
edge-us-west-2 -> lon-edge-proxy : 312ms
lon-edge-proxy -> eu-west-2-serving : 780ms
eu-west-2-serving -> edge-us-west-2 (return) : 100ms
TOTAL ~1210ms
```

carla (platform): I can see the router policy hit a fallback. Route-policy v2 has a "regional-burst-fallback" that kicks in when healthy_capacity_estimate for us-west-2 < 12%. Autoscaler logs show a spike + slow scale-up due to a transient quota error at 18:21:27. The router then routed eligible requests to the "regional-mirror" in eu-west-2.

ben (runtime): Runtime logs show KV-cache shard rebalance for gpt-variant-3.large around the same time, which temporarily degraded local throughput. Coupled with the autoscaler delay that explains why the router decided to fallback cross-region.

raj (sre): Useful. Two actionables: reproduce with a pinned header, and add short-term sticky routing for ACME. Can you share a repro curl we can run?

ben (runtime): Repro curl (use an internal test token):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer TEST_ACME_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-variant-3.large","input":"hello"}'
```
Run that repeatedly (~50 qps) and you'll see some requests proxied to eu-west-2 when local capacity is exhausted. To force strictly-local routing for the customer, include header `X-Redwood-Force-Local: 1` (internal only) — temporary mitigation.

jamie (support): Shared mitigations with ACME: they added the X-Redwood-Region header and verified p99 dropped back to ~90ms for their test traffic. They're asking why the platform didn't scale faster.

carla (platform): Scaling was delayed because the cloud quota request timed out (we hit a soft limit on ephemeral GPUs in us-west-2). I've opened cloud-quota-urgent with infra@cloud (ticket CLOUD-2026-998). Patch: change fallback threshold from 12% -> 8% for next deploy so we favor local replicas slightly more aggressively; but still want safe fallback to avoid errors.

raj (sre): For follow-up: 1) add telemetry alert for cross-region fallback rate > 0.5% per minute per customer, 2) add an annotation on the trace UI showing which fallback rule fired, 3) review autoscaler cooldown to avoid oscillation. I'll file tasks. :memo:

carla (platform): Also FYI billing: fallback to eu-west-2 counts as normal serving region usage (no double-billing). I've looped in jess (finance) to confirm ACME won't be surprised.

jamie (support): Customer update: they accepted the temporary header patch and want a root-cause update. I'll keep them posted. +:thumbsup:

ben (runtime): One more datapoint — KV cache rebalance logs show re-sharding because a node reported high memory pressure; I'll investigate whether we can make rebalance less aggressive during scale events.

raj (sre): Thanks all. I'll own the follow-up checklist and post ETA here. For now mark INC-2026-437 as "mitigated - temporary route pin applied". :eyes:

jamie (support): Closing loop with ACME: they confirmed latency normalized after we applied the header and after the autoscaler finished scaling at 18:24Z. I'll add the final note to the incident and send the RCA draft when ready.

support-bot: INC-2026-437 status -> mitigated (18:31Z)
